titulo: Space Agencies Report Increased Risk of Space Rock Striking Earth in 2032

fuente.licencia: Dominio público (VOA, gobierno de EE. UU.)
fuente.nota: Text shortened by paragraphs; sentences unchanged.

parrafos: Recent calculations suggest there is a small chance - perhaps around 1 to 3 percent - the space rock 2024 YR4 will hit Earth in 2032. This also means there is around a 97 to 99 percent chance it will safely pass our planet in that year. The odds of a strike will likely continue to go up and down as the asteroid’s path around the sun is better understood.

NASA and the European Space Agency’s Webb Space Telescope will observe this near-Earth asteroid in March before the object becomes impossible to see. Once that happens, scientists will have to wait until 2028 when it passes our way again.
There are millions of asteroids orbiting the sun between Mars and Jupiter. That area is known as the main asteroid belt. The asteroids sometimes get pushed out of the belt and can end up elsewhere.

A telescope in Chile discovered the asteroid 2024 YR4 in late December. It is estimated to measure between 40 and 90 meters across. NASA said observations by the Webb space telescope should provide a more exact measurement.

At first, NASA and the European Space Agency put the odds of a strike at just over one percent. But later calculations suggested the odds had risen to 2 or even 3 percent. NASA described the likelihood of a strike as “extremely low.”
Until scientists have a better understanding of the asteroid’s path around the sun, they warned that the odds will continue to change — and quite possibly fall to zero.

“You don’t have to be worried about anything. It’s a curiosity,” said Larry Denneau. He is a software engineer at the University of Hawaii working with ATLAS, a program to identify asteroids that might endanger Earth. That effort first spotted the asteroid. Denneau said, “Don’t panic. Let the process play out, and we’ll have a for-sure answer.”

In 2021, NASA said another possibly worrisome asteroid, Apophis, did not present a risk to Earth. NASA made the announcement after additional telescope observations ruled out any chance of it hitting Earth in 2068.

Paul Chodas is director of NASA’s Center for Near-Earth Object Studies. Chodas said in an email to the Associated Press, “No one should be concerned that the impact probability is rising. This is the behavior our team expected.”

Since the asteroid’s size and orbit are uncertain, it is unclear where it might hit and what the possible effects would be should it strike Earth. ESA said, if the asteroid is smaller, the effect might be similar to the Tunguska event that flattened thousands of square kilometers of forest in Siberia in 1908. But if the asteroid is larger, close to 100 meters, the effects “would be significantly worse.”
Chodas said once the Webb telescope measures the asteroid’s size, NASA can predict “how serious an impact this asteroid could produce and how difficult a task it might be to deflect this asteroid.”

NASA already has some experience moving an asteroid. The space agency’s Dart spacecraft hit a harmless asteroid in 2022. This was the first planetary defense test of its kind, changing the asteroid’s orbit around its larger companion asteroid.
titulo_es: Space agencies report an increased risk of an asteroid hitting Earth in 2032
resumen_es: The probability that asteroid 2024 YR4 will hit Earth in 2032 has risen to 1–3 %, but NASA and ESA are calling for calm because the figure will change as its orbit becomes better known.
nivel_motivo: The measured vocabulary level rises because of proper names and astronomical terms, but the text is clear and simply structured: B2.

ideas_clave.idea: There is roughly a one-to-three percent chance that asteroid 2024 YR4 will strike Earth in 2032, a figure expected to fluctuate.
The Webb telescope will observe it in March before it disappears from view until 2028.
Discovered in Chile in December, the rock measures 40 to 90 metres and, like millions of others, may have been pushed out of the main asteroid belt.
The estimated risk has risen from about one to as much as three percent, but experts call it extremely low and say it may well drop to zero.
Specialists urge calm, recalling that Apophis was later ruled out as a threat and that a rising probability is normal at this stage.
Possible damage depends on the asteroid's size, ranging from a Tunguska-type event to much worse, and measuring it will show how hard it would be to deflect.
NASA has already shown, with its 2022 DART mission, that it can change an asteroid's orbit.

resumen_modelo: The text reports that, according to recent calculations, asteroid 2024 YR4 has a small probability, between one and three percent, of striking Earth in 2032, which means it will very likely pass safely. Detected by a telescope in Chile in December and estimated to be between 40 and 90 metres wide, the rock will be observed by the Webb Space Telescope in March, before it becomes invisible until 2028. Although the estimated risk has risen from just over one percent, NASA describes it as extremely low, and experts insist that the figure will keep changing as the asteroid's orbit is better understood and may even fall to zero. Indeed, specialists call for calm, recalling that Apophis was eventually ruled out as a threat and stressing that the current increase was expected. Should an impact occur, its consequences would depend on the object's size: a smaller asteroid might cause damage similar to the 1908 Tunguska event in Siberia, whereas one close to 100 metres would be considerably more destructive. Measuring it precisely will also indicate how difficult deflecting it would be, a task for which NASA already has some experience since its 2022 DART mission.
